info.description: Supported profile: W3C SD-JWT+KB, ES256, DCQL literal full subject paths with explicit issuer/definition/version policy, decentralized_identifier request client ID, direct_post vp_token. Ephemeral sessions/cache, persistent encrypted Rust identity. Container/public distribution and physical observations are separately recorded. Stable codes and limitations are documented in README. Optional durable generic issuer: pre-authorized-code, vc+sd-jwt, ES256, recipient-bound JWK proof and accredited wallet-instance attestation. App-local PostgreSQL ledger; independently pinned registry authority. Other issuance grants/formats are unsupported. Scalar verification uses six common credworks_scalar fields plus exactly one legacy key-ID or bounded authenticated credential-key set. Upgrade consumers before enabling sets. Generic schema and exact paths come from authenticated immutable registered definitions. Education behavior remains unchanged when scalar config is absent.

get.description: Stored ES256 oauth-authz-req+jwt. Exact Education DCQL, decentralized_identifier client ID, vp_token, direct_post, nonce/state, fixed creation plus120-second maximum expiry. Retrieval never extends expiry. Capability is public ceremony data, never application correlation. Retrieval additionally enforces current exact permission and cache freshness before returning the unchanged signed request. Scalar mode supplies authenticated definition-derived DCQL with credworks_scalar as documented by the CredWorksScalarRequestExtension schema. Scalar requests additionally retain their original cache/authority/permission/status deadline across refresh; set requests cap signed exp to that minimum. Each session freezes allowed issuer IDs/public pins; refresh can withdraw, never add members. Generic scalar/structured compact Request Objects fit the 262144-byte consumer cap. The approved 64-path, 16-component profile can exceed 65536 bytes; legacy/DID transport caps remain separate.

post.description: Protected local-runtime continuation. Both issuer and verifier roles are required. Atomically links a permitted completed verification to one holder-bound scalar offer. Exact capability, interaction and identical issuance payload authorize retries, including after committed lost replies and restart. Issuer and holder are server-derived; arbitrary remote verifier references, public state and caller holder fields cannot authorize issuance. Effective offer/token expiry cannot exceed the original session/evidence/credential deadline. Current exact source key/scope/permission/status and output issuer authority are rechecked through issuance. The seven-field wallet request and public accepted ACK remain unchanged. Code redemption remains one-time; lost token replies are fail-closed.
